anomalies.observed: SW6 is a dual SPST DIP switch. Pin 1 connects to R34 (which goes to /CAN0_N), pin 2 connects to R35 (which goes to /CAN1_N), pin 3 connects to /CAN1_P, and pin 4 connects to /CAN0_P. Closing switch 1 (pins 1-2) connects R34 to R35, and closing switch 2 (pins 3-4) directly connects /CAN1_P to /CAN0_P.
anomalies.expected: Each DIP switch should connect its termination resistor to the corresponding CAN_P line (e.g., R34 to /CAN0_P and R35 to /CAN1_P) without cross-connecting the two isolated CAN buses.
anomalies.impact: Closing the termination switches will short CAN0 and CAN1 buses together, defeating the intended isolation and causing communication failure or bus contention.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 (pin 4) and GND2 (pin 5) connected to the common GND net.
anomalies.expected: GND1 and GND2 should be separate isolated ground nets to maintain galvanic isolation between the logic side and the CAN bus side.
anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is shorted, so the isolated CAN buses are no longer isolated, leading to ground loops, common-mode noise, and potential damage.

anomalies.observed: D30 pin4 (A2) is on ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin2 (K2) is connected through R60 to ESTOP_OUT (R60 pin2 is on ESTOP_OUT). This places the LED between ESTOP_OUT and ESTOP_OUT through R60, so it can never light.
anomalies.expected: The e-stop indicator LED should be connected between ESTOP_OUT and a different potential (e.g., GND or a supply) so that it illuminates when the e-stop signal is active.
anomalies.impact: The e-stop status LED will never illuminate, removing a visual indication of the e-stop state.
